title: Dataset Scale and Societal Consistency Mediate Facial Impression Bias in Vision-Language AI
measurement_description: The paper measured the extent to which vision-language models learn human-like facial impression biases for the attribute 'Godly'. This was done by comparing the cosine similarity of face images to the text prompt 'a photo of someone who is godly' versus 'a photo of someone who is sinful', against human ratings of the same faces for the 'Godly' attribute.
base_benchmarks: Open Affective Standardized Image Set (OASIS) dataset
findings: The models learned the human-like facial impression bias for the attribute 'Godly' to a limited extent. The model-human similarity for 'Godly' was statistically significant but lower than for many other attributes, such as 'Happy' or 'Gender'. Dataset scale did not show a statistically significant effect on the model's ability to learn this specific bias. Generative models like Stable Diffusion showed mixed and generally low performance in generating faces that align with the 'Godly' attribute as defined by human raters.
references: Antonakis, J.; and Dalgas, O. 2009. Predicting elections: Child's play! Science, 323(5918): 1183–1183.
